newsitem.title: USA: L.A. Mayor mulls plan to return $31 mln to airport.
newsitem.headline: L.A. Mayor mulls plan to return $31 mln to airport.

text.p: Los Angeles Mayor Richard Riordan will decide within 10 days whether to return $31 million to the city airports department to settle a heated dispute with federal authorities, his office said Thursday.
The Los Angeles City Council voted Wednesday to return the $31 million to the Los Angeles Department of Airports, and asked the mayor to approve the transfer.
"The mayor is going to take a really close look at it over the next 10 days," Steve Sugerman, deputy to the mayor, said Thursday.
Earlier this year, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered Los Angeles to return the $31 million, arguing that federal law requires airport revenues to be spent on airport operations.
Until the city repays the money, the FAA said it would freeze $60 million in federal grants for capital improvements at four airports that Los Angeles operates.
Last November, the Los Angeles City Council voted to hold the funds in a city trust account until the issue was resolved.
